messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@globalmed.com>, Priya Iyer <priya.iyer@globalmed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: GlobalMed private VPC / on-prem requirements & next steps

Hi Sanjay / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move toward an architecture review and pilot. Please flag anything I missed.

High-level pain / drivers you shared:
- Data residency & regulatory: PHI handling requires customer-controlled key management and audit logs.
- Network restrictions: no general internet egress from inference hosts; only approved outbound channels.
- Air-gap consideration: some workloads will need an isolated environment (air-gapped) for certain regions.
- Latency & locality: inference needs to be colocated in your primary US-East region to meet SLAs for clinician tools.

Goals we agreed on:
- Confirm deployment model options (Private VPC vs. on-prem air-gapped installer).
- Run an architecture review with your infra/security leads to validate ports, peering, and KMS flow.
- Kick off a 60-day pilot on a scoped dataset after architecture sign-off.

Constraints / technical notes from Redwood:
- Private VPC option: managed control plane in our cloud with private connectivity (AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering). Minimal outbound egress required for control-plane telemetry and updates when opted in.
- Air-gapped on-prem: we have an on-prem installer for fully isolated deployments; control plane can be self-hosted and we provide tooling for offline updates.
- KMS: we support customer-managed KMS (Cloud KMS/HSM) and can integrate for envelope encryption; we will provide audit logs for requests.

Immediate next steps:
1) You to share the current network diagram and list of constrained IP ranges (attachment or link).
2) Schedule architecture review with your infra/security: propose Mon/Tue next week (I suggested times below).
3) Redwood to send draft SOW and pre-auth checklist (attached draft SOW).

Attachments: GlobalMed_Network_Diagram.pdf (placeholder), Redwood_Private_Deployment_SOW_v1.docx

Proposed times for architecture review (PT):
- Mon Jun 21 10:00–11:00 PT
- Tue Jun 22 08:00–09:00 PT

Thanks — happy to adjust.
\Best,
Camila Reyes

Thanks Sanjay — great, Mon Jun 21 10:00 PT is locked on our side.

Quick answers to your bullets to prep Priya and the security team:

- Air-gapped on-prem installer: yes — we support a fully isolated installation. Updates are handled via an offline package process: Redwood provides signed update bundles that your infra team uploads to the appliance. No outbound connectivity is required for runtime. (We will provide the offline update guide in the arch review.)

- Managed control plane (Private VPC): we can avoid public IP exposure by using AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering. In that model, telemetry and control-plane communication flow over the private link. If you require, we can also evaluate a customer-hosted control plane for additional isolation.

- Required network considerations (high level; arch review will finalize):
  - PrivateLink / peering: TCP 443 for control-plane API over PrivateLink (no public endpoint).
  - KMS: outbound to your KMS endpoints only (TLS 443). For on-prem with HSM, we support direct connectivity to your HSM appliance over allowed network paths.
  - Storage: S3-compatible object store access for model artifacts (can be internal S3 endpoint via VPC).
  - Management VM access: we recommend limiting SSH (22) to jump hosts for maintenance; not required for runtime.

I have attached the draft SOW and a short pre-auth checklist for your team. We'll bring an engineer with air-gap deployment experience to the call (Connor O'Brien) and Marissa will cover pilot scoping.

Attachments: Redwood_Private_Deployment_SOW_v1.docx
\See you Monday — invite sent.
\Cheers,
Camila
\--
